notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#19
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone! Here’s the latest update on several key systems in the game.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/0f7698d12162b6b1f5c9e910f0708cfaa0d3d0c5.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/f611dfe87b00ed9185facadfdb931b5e099b80a6.png"][/img][/p][p]First, I’ve begun constructing a variety of space station types. Players will encounter industrial bases built on rocky asteroids, research outposts on icy asteroids, and large hub ports serving as regional centers—along with many other styles of space structures. These environments will provide diverse battlefields for players to engage with.[/p][p][/p][p]Next, I’ve fully rebuilt the game’s unlock system. As a roguelike, meta-progression are tied to process-based unlocks. We’ve now established a more universal framework for feature unlocks. Currently, the Ship Store is the first to adopt this new system, and it will gradually extend to more game mechanics in the future.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/f68b6005e8542e8ae74c732411da0afceac92289.png"][/img][/p][p]Lastly, introducing the all-new Crafting System. This system is a core part of the roguelike meta-progression and directly supports warship loadout gameplay. Players will be able to use resources earned in-game to craft permanent ship equipment. At the same time, craftable equipment will be progressively unlocked as you advance.[/p][p]That is all for this dev log. Thank you for your on going support! be sure to share the news with other commanders![/p][p]See you next time![/p]

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#18
notes.notes: [p align="start"]Hello everyone, welcome back to the latest development log. We have introduced [b]Cruise Mode[/b], which is designed to streamline travel between encounter points.[/p][p align="start"]We noticed that moving between encounters became increasingly frustrating as complexity ramped up, especially when dealing with vertical elevation changes.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/9851eb72213d0c9010a6d585b94d2a85fd6c29ee.png"][/img][/p][p align="start"]In this mode, your ship will achieve a higher forward speed at the cost of reduced maneuverability. The controls work similarly to mouse-based steering commonly found in space combat games. Note that all weapons are temporarily disabled while Cruise Mode is active, and entering this mode requires clear space ahead with no nearby hostiles.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/4b402b2a6575ac24807544945240d48c44f3a0e5.png"][/img][/p][p align="start"]On the environment side, we are continuously building out zone visuals throughout the system, aiming to meet the foundational needs for a complete gameplay experience.[/p][p align="start"]Several optimizations have also been made. We’ve improved visual effects for mining and gas harvesting, enhanced the level info interface, and introduced a new progress-scoring system for clearing encounter zones. The reason behind adjusting the clearance mechanic is that with the increased number of encounters, relying solely on one or two key events to complete a level sometimes didn’t feel right.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/aa52d4cec447f53a7f8018d4d1880cd64530526c.png"][/img][/p][p align="start"]In combat, enemy AI now features squad-based behavior: when one unit engages, the entire squad responds in sync, boosting both coordination and intensity.[/p][p align="start"]That’s all for this dev log. Thank you for your ongoing support—be sure to share the news with other commanders![/p][p align="start"]See you next time![/p]

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#17
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p]Our flagship title's Wishlist has now surpassed 5,000! Thank you all for your incredible support.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/870dc85b7ed7e63d169e25039eacc11bd38fe85c.png"][/img][/p][p]Today, we're sharing progress on optimizations and gameplay updates focused on the [b]Encounter Zone[/b] experience. Our core goal is to enhance the depth and variety within these zones, tackling underutilized space while improving how information is delivered to players. This means enabling quicker understanding of the environment and decision-making upon entering an Encounter Zone. This work is ongoing, and we plan to validate its effectiveness by building several representative Encounter Zones.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/487de0a8b5db370945b3913473b9f2a9daa4e107.png"][/img][/p][p]Significant adjustments have been made to the [b]encounter mechanics[/b]. Points of Interest within Encounter Zones now support [b]multiple encounter events[/b], and some encounters can exist independently of specific points. We've also introduced a new [b]encounter classification system[/b], which lays the groundwork for layered information display on the map interface.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/aed7c8ab4e8e6e67197fe149ecb0ed48fa784c5e.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Combat encounters[/b] have seen several key refinements. Basic combat now features [b]pre-spawned enemy units[/b], and we've added [b]three new dynamic encounter types[/b]: [b]Reinforcement Units[/b] spawning after a delay, [b]Ambush Units[/b] triggered by player actions, and interactive [b]Raid Targets[/b] like neutral freighters with their escort fleets. Outside of combat, these freighters and escorts now use a [b]streamlined formation system[/b] for coordinated movement. Importantly, all enemy units now exhibit [b]basic idle movement[/b], so they no longer stand idle waiting for players. The combat reward system has also been rebuilt around [b]physical entity drops[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/d8d02e21f2fb0968c00b2bc372656ea677a14aec.png"][/img][/p][p]Other updates include the introduction of new [b]mining and localized resource collection gameplay[/b], along with selecting a specific Encounter Zone as a [b]testbed for visual environment improvements[/b]. Finally, to address information overload, the [b]HUD system[/b] has been overhauled to [b]dynamically scale information intensity[/b] based on target distance and player focus, significantly [b]reducing interface noise[/b].[/p][p]That wraps up this development update! Thank you for your continued support of[b] The Flagship[/b]. Please feel free to share this news.[/p][p]Until next time.[/p]

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#16
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone.[/p][p]Our focus has recently shifted to building the core roguelike features, particularly the levels, and this will be the main theme for our upcoming logs.[/p][p]We've completely rewritten the stage structure, moving from a linear room design to a more [i]Slay the Spire[/i]-like system, where each node is not just a fight or event but a small, explorable space. This change allows players to make more informed, tactical decisions when choosing their path.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/750a5b0108ffcf66d4983331a31e938ddc011360.jpg"][/img][/p][p]To complement our new roguelike room design, we’ve also reworked the teleportation process. Currently, our team is discussing two potential approaches: one where you select your destination and teleport directly, and another where the destination selection is integrated into the teleportation process itself. Both options have their pros and cons, and we’re still weighing our choices.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/c60c5fa5af7621b3fa29f612b866eda7802ec718.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Additionally, we’ve introduced a hyperspace accelerator mechanic inspired by [i]EVE Online[/i]. This new traversal method could be incorporated into specific rooms in the future, adding more variety to the game’s movement mechanics.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/2035d008d7bf226784a852bd9e549281226a74f4.jpg"][/img][/p][p]That's all for today. Thank you for your support, and feel free to share this update with more friends. See you next time![/p]

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#15
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone![img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/f38184fcbb4ab94d0dab3bb885eb6659380c597b.jpg"][/img][/p][p]In today’s update, we’ve introduced several exciting improvements. First, we’ve completely revamped the equipment interface to make it more intuitive. By highlighting key attributes and streamlining the design, players can now access critical information faster than ever before. The equipment operation process has also been optimized for greater efficiency.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/feadee34baa544e4b8df38a1149a3a1d36db18a2.jpg"][/img][/p][p]On the combat side, we’ve made point-defense systems more intuitive. They now distribute targets when facing multiple threats, significantly boosting their tactical value. Additionally, we’ve added a tactical settings feature that allows players to fine-tune their point-defense systems based on projectile behavior, enabling more optimized firing patterns.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/6fde5b41827d146c330bb1cfa4683a32edba1b7c.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Our AI system has also seen some notable enhancements. The IFF logic has been improved, and neutral units will now actively retaliate when attacked, with support for multiple engagement conditions.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/054507c3981072a9e5ff95c0220a3ca541947892.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Visually, we’ve polished the spawning effects of regional fleets to make their appearance feel more seamless. Projectiles now gradually shrink and weaken as they travel, resulting in a more natural disappearance effect.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s all for today’s development log. Thank you for your continued support and feedback. Feel free to share with more friends, and we’ll catch you next time![/p]

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#14
notes.notes: [p]Greetings, everyone! [/p][p]Enemy ships can now launch missiles, and we’ve improved the AI to enable this functionality. Additionally, point-defense systems have been upgraded to counter incoming missiles—Though ships can't shake missiles with quick maneuvers, taking them out first is your best bet – and now you can![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/ba798c645de5cd1b6856062b7ff80b10c3314a67.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve also refined the HUD design for clarity, especially in displaying damage more clearly. Based on community feedback, we’ve changed the circular shield and armor indicators to symmetrical, shortened bars to avoid directional misunderstandings.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/46f29a225a71884bc7bc3b2d5b55e344c869ab05.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The equipment interface has been streamlined, grouping similar items to reduce clutter and making it easier to find what you need. Detailed info and comparison features are now included.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/88c55492d1c89d9936b863cd521db35f17edfdd1.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve fixed several bugs, including scaling ratio issues and loading screen problems, and further optimized turret targeting logic.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s all for today. [i]Flagship[/i] has now been in development for one full year. Thank you for your continued support and feedback—we couldn’t improve without you. Feel free to share with friends, and see you next time![/p]

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#13
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone! We’ve reached another milestone with over 3,000 Steam Wishlists—thank you for your incredible support! Your feedback has been instrumental in helping us improve the game.[/p][p] To enable the creation of larger environments while avoiding visual anomalies, we’ve completely overhauled the galaxy scale system.the previous scale, inspired by "Rebel Galaxy" felt cartoonish, . We decided to scale planets up by 10 times, and in some cases, even more.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/03d850844cef6c5d39c06eb312dcf76631b4fe8b.jpg"][/img][/p][p]To support this, we’ve reworked the FloatingOrigin system and shrunk the entire game world by 1000 times. This massive adjustment affects nearly every aspect of the game, improving how we manage spatial information and enhancing the galaxy editor for future development.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/675732b82b2ed9eb882df1f6a2a62bc47acfbab6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve also enhanced weapon sound effects, fine-tuning volumes and adding new control features for a better overall experience. Additionally, we’ve fixed key issues, including interaction functionality, missile switching problems, and frame rate settings.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/02c2bdef3820e4cff1c5f27067a6fe95477c9807.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve also addressed several issues, including a major overhaul of the interaction functionality, resolving the issue where players couldn’t switch weapons after running out of missiles, and fixing the frame rate setting in the options menu.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s all for this update. Thank you for your continued support of "Flagship." See you next time![/p]

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#12
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone! Over the past two weeks, we have focused on optimizing and improving several aspects of the game.[/p][p]First,For ship turrets we added level of detail and fixed lighting issues making them look more natural under different conditions.Additionally, we optimized the proximity fuse for Flak turrets to boost their efficiency. while high firing rate weapons now perform better by firing multiple times within a single frame, delivering a better C.I.W.S style firing effects. Missile trails have also been refined to provide a more intuitive visual.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/033ab336a9ea676ec9745aea4a4a705587f2a558.png"][/img][/p][p]We also improved the main turret aiming camera by addressing the limited vertical aim range. Now, when aiming near the boundaries the camera will slightly rotate to provide a wider view, enhancing aiming flexibility.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/732b633b7ba3fad06e9dce95168b4bc27caa59a9.png"][/img][/p][p]For ship repair interface,Players can now better understand how repair amounts and costs relate. and have more control over ship repair.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/1cf44e1581f3d9cab214ebaa92af80fdbffd1c67.jpg"][/img][/p][p]On the audio front, we are experimenting with new background music styles to find a better fit.We have also added dynamic music transitions based on combat states for deeper immersion.And fixed an issue where music would occasionally stop playing.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/e4ab75c5ee30d91775d2a1fac2b803446cb9cb6e.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Thats all for this update. Thanks for supporting " The Flagship" and stay tuned for more![/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="2enp_YPBpxI;full"][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#11
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, and welcome to this devlog for The Flagship.

Starting with fire control system optimizations: We've rectified trajectory prediction algorithms in subturrets, achieving measurable accuracy improvements while stabilizing target acquisition protocols. For main cannon operations, we resolved target lock disruption during multi-object proximity scenarios, along with trajectory deflection issues caused by obstructive celestial bodies. Sustained firing sequences of main cannons will now maintain consistent, even with turret not valid for firing.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/80d25bee2a9cf61deaa4ea48e5e58428c1d961f2.jpg[/img]

In equipment adjustments, we've introduced the tractor beam - a dedicated module for managing item retrieval properties. The afterburner mechanism has been redesigned to utilize percentage-based acceleration, eliminating insufficient thrust scenarios while enhancing maneuverability for smoother handling. Notably, equipment management now features a context-sensitive module list adjacent to target slots, streamlining the configuration process.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/2d249e65b50925fb37da8773adf6f077cb9c43ae.jpg[/img]

Performance optimizations include redesigned battleship blueprint loading systems. By minimizing redundant calls, we've achieved approximately 10x performance improvements with significantly reduced stuttering, alongside fixes for potential equipment disappearance glitches.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/8b76f9e29e286cb749bc9f108c29f8a234d50276.jpg[/img]
Regarding gameplay validation demo,  we've refined key encounter node placements to ensure better player guidance through each nodes.In-game store has also been repaired to enhance overall experience.

That's all for this development log update. Thank you for your continued support and attention to The Flagship. We’ll see you next time!

[previewyoutube=Ooirj1qCZIs;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#10
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, and welcome to the dev log for The Flagship. Over the past two weeks, we've focused on building a prototype level experience. Here are the key updates:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/588df04c11cb5b9d7062b2830f7bf3273705cb25.jpg[/img]
We've introduced a Radar (Detector) equipment module, allowing players to adjust their ship's detection range through gear configuration. The signal source system has been rebuilt and now features a universal HUD type that marks interactable objects, portals, and collectibles. Specifically for Treasure Container Signal Towers, unlocked containers will be permanently displayed on the HUD.

The Faction Systemhas been upgraded to a dynamic mechanism. Faction relationship values now support permanent storage and multi-condition modifications. A key implementation: opening guarded faction containerswill immediately trigger hostility from that faction, enabling behavior-driven combat encounters.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/a320af9e5fddf15280f9c712d6183f08e283a2a4.jpg[/img]
We've added fixed turret platforms to the combat roster. These share functional logic with fighter craft but remain immobile, making them ideal for base defense or level garrison scenarios.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/49397eecd5f208ad92ea46089bcf5fe412b18a5d.jpg[/img]
A lite Quest System has entered preliminary testing. A simplified quest status panel has been added to the main interface, providing guidance for certain encounters. Note this is a temporary solution that will undergo structural changes as gameplay expands.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/1b9819060b2dac9462620cdd05a12b0484ed94ed.jpg[/img]
Finally, we are constructing a short validation level using existing systems. This level will serve as the core demo experience for testing system compatibility and gameplay experience. 

That's all for this development update! Thank you for your continued support of Flagship! See you next time!

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#9
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, and welcome to the dev log for The Flagship.
First and foremost, we’ve overhauled our node and encounter system. Previously, a challenge run would guide players through a series of nodes, each featuring a single encounter—whether that was a battle, puzzle, or another event. While this structure works well for many roguelike games, it didn’t quite fit  The Flagship A space battleship simulator cannot exist without exploration.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/f88d80e528fb5ead59c7a176fd46e61baf6c8b65.jpg[/img]
In the new system, each node now supports multiple types of encounters, such as combat, treasure chests, or other gameplay elements. While key encounters remain essential for progression, optional ones allow players to explore at their own pace, uncovering hidden secrets and experiencing a greater sense of adventure. This redesign not only enriches each node but also introduces a layer of randomized exploration, adding depth and variety to your journey. While this change complicates node configuration, it unlocks a universe of possibilities for dynamic and engaging gameplay.
To complement these changes, we’re refining other related systems, starting with the AI. NPCs now have more complex behaviors beyond just combat
On the mini-games front, we’ve implemented several core features to test these new mechanisms. For instance, players can now interact with destructible crates or unlock hidden rewards.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/e836ccd9af62e3696b74c968f1079b54eb5786d8.jpg[/img]
We’ve also introduced the afterburner booster as a new type of equipment item. Players can now customize their speed and maneuverability by equipping different booster types. Additionally, we’ve streamlined the combat interface by switching to an icon-based weapon display. This change frees up screen space for critical information while creating a cleaner, more organized layout that helps you stay focused on the action.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/24ce083fb167eda3ffc2b127b137bd949b9f94f0.png[/img]
That's all for this dev log. Thank you for your support and attention to The Flagship. Until next time!

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#8
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, and welcome to the new devlog for The Flagship. In this update, we’re focusing on further refining our equipment and outfitting systems.

First off, we’ve introduced the concept of "size" to our equipment. Weapons and other gear will now have specific size attributes that correlate with the requirements of the ships they’re equipped on. This change allows us to better balance the visual size between ships and turret models while also opening up more possibilities for the outfitting system. We’ve already set up some test weapons with varying sizes, and we’ll continue to refine the design as we move forward.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/df78533bb1db7b40bd98c0235da93092b7d4dce2.png[/img]
Next, we’ve removed the restriction that limited players to purchasing a single ship hull only once. Alongside this, we’ve developed an entirely new ship blueprint system, which reduces the barriers for players looking to switch up their playstyles. To support these changes, we’ve added a new test ship and are currently organizing the relevant configuration tools. As we accelerate our feature iterations, we’ve realized that our existing support tools and production pipelines need to be updated to ensure efficiency remains on track.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/947480a62cce5a8edf23096dec10d9e792f77464.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/1ac7f12173c8e16b6fa3b766f690cd678f875d56.png[/img]
On the user experience front, we’re working on improving the visual clarity of the game at 1080p resolution. Based on feedback from our players, we identified that text readability at 1080p was a significant concern. To better understand the issue firsthand, I purchased a used 1080p monitor, and after testing, the problem became clear. We’re now optimizing UI elements one by one, aiming to enhance the visual experience without compromising usability.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/21d1736f0df208d9805e93b9bb8cd76ba2072e46.png[/img]
That’s the main focus of this development log. Thank you all for your continued support and feedback—your input has been invaluable to our progress. We’re committed to bringing you a better gaming experience in the days ahead. If you have any suggestions or ideas, please don’t hesitate to share them in the comments below. We’re always listening and striving to improve. Thank you, and until next time!

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog#7
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, and welcome to the new devlog for The Flagship. In this update, we’re focusing on enhancing your in-station experience.

First, we’ve made significant improvements to in-station ship display. Your weapons will now load and display correctly, allowing you to visually inspect your weapon configurations before entering combat. Additionally, we’ve given players the ability to freely rotate the camera within the station, so you can finally take a moment to enjoy your warship.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/2c88958cc0b926027968c0bafd03b876ccf3d6cd.png[/img]

Next, we’ve streamlined and optimized the equipment system. We’ve introduced a categorization feature to the inventory, making it easier to manage your gear. Equipped items are now removed directly from the inventory instead of being merely marked, providing a more intuitive management experience. Moreover, we’ve simplified the equipment process itself. Players can now select an item from the inventory, then use the Tab key to switch between equipment slots, and press R to equip it, greatly reducing the number of steps required. We’ve also added a comparison feature; by pressing the Alt key, you can bring up a comparison interface to help you choose the best equipment for your needs. Furthermore, sub-turrets now include an focus shot, allowing you to preview your weapon configuration. The missile ship section is no longer limited to increasing the number of projectiles but now also supports expanding the variety of missiles you can equip.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/846c27c79d3707bb8514c2c5380887a180373ffb.png[/img]

In terms of warship management, this update introduces a major new feature: players can now own multiple ships! Currently, only one ship per hull type can be owned, but this still provides greater freedom for players to explore different playstyles without needing to reconfigure their equipment and settings. However, managing multiple ships will consume more resources, including credits and minerals, adding a new layer of strategy to your gameplay experience.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/c95d84fbd8e6324dddcf7d4b74807a4977328669.png[/img]

We’ve introduced a new energy management. The weapon systems for the main cannons and wing guns will now have their own independent energy pools, making firepower sustainability an important factor in your equipment choices. Other systems will also be updated with energy-related changes in future updates, and we’ll share more details as they develop.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/48a0de6013b9bc28defcefb79944795c823c8146.png[/img]

Finally, we’ve made some smaller optimizations to the combat experience. The firing logic for the main ship weapons is now more intuitive—simply single-click to fire. The missile launching mechanism has also been improved; players can now launch the desired number of missiles with just a few clicks, while holding the button down will unleash a volley over a fixed duration, making the process more convenient than ever before.
That’s all for this update. Thank you for your attention and support. We’ll see you next time!

notes.title: The Flagship Devlog #6
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, and welcome to the new devlog for The Flagship. In this update, we’re focusing on further optimizing the combat experience.
First, We made more optimizations to the main cannon shooting mechanics. To enhance the experience of engaging small targets, we’ve implemented a series of improvements. We’ve introduced a new reticle snapping feature, which performed exceptionally well in initial tests and significantly improved accuracy against small targets. Additionally, we’ve refined the soft-locking mechanism, constraining target selection within a specific range to prevent counterintuitive outcomes. To further validate these improvements, we’ve also included long-range weapons in our shooting experience tests, ensuring the overall shooting mechanics are more polished.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/87c3fee9d37e5c8a7a031903c8bbb9698d77aefe.png[/img]
Next, we’ve updated the shield system. We’ve added visual effects for shield hits, making combat more intuitive. The manual shield’s visual representation has also been changed to a spherical display with independent hit detection, providing players with more precise defensive feedback.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/f9590063489b3951e88099ea12962dc86c3657a2.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/76c88ad8f5c6a63cbe7cf0d224d4113b668d846e.png[/img]
In terms of broadside firing,or directed firing, we’ve adjusted the laser reticle to support charge aiming. This means side firing is no longer just about mindless hits but now emphasizes skill and strategy. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/4f38d7d40356457c7f919b9f5aa9f5d2c4b8731c.png[/img]
Additionally, we’ve added a chaotic shooting trait to directed firing when targeting locked enemies, Make shooting feel less repetitive
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/f70907097b381a56a6769656726055e46f46a870.png[/img]

The missile system has also received significant updates. We’ve incorporated predictive tracking capabilities into the tracking algorithm, with certain missiles now utilizing this higher-hit-rate tracking method to improve overall combat efficiency. Regarding the firing mechanism, we’ve simplified the controls: single-tap to fire one missile, double-tap to launch a full salvo. This makes the operation more intuitive and reduces unnecessary distractions. 
For subturrets, we’ve expanded their range by adding a CIWS-style close-range vulcan, a long-range pulse laser, and a long range flak. Subturrets also inherit the chaotic shooting trait.
Finally, we’ve added tutorial instructions to help new players get up to speed faster. These tutorials are accessible from the pause menu under “Tutorials” and currently cover the basics of movement, offensive tactics, and survival concepts.
We hope you’ll enjoy these changes. If you have any feedback or suggestions, please share them in the comments. Thank you all for your support. We’ll continue to work hard to refine and enhance the gaming experience.

notes.title: TheFlagship Devlog#5
notes.notes:
Hello everyone, in this update, we’re bringing several important changes that directly respond to your feedback and expectations.
First, let’s talk about the vertical mobility of warships. Many of you have questioned whether combat in the game is limited to 2D after watching previous videos. Based on your feedback and survey responses, we’ve decided to introduce vertical mobility for warships. It’s important to note that while the game’s overall design still focuses on a Rebel Galaxy like combat, we’ve adopted an approach similar to Dreadnought, offering limited vertical movement without including rolling or pitching. Rolling and pitching will only serve as visual feedback to enhance the sense of movement. Additionally, we’ve added vertical position indicators for other units on the radar, and a simple altitude gauge has been placed on the left side of the screen to help players better grasp the battlefield’s spatial dimensions.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/3bb58d8799ca97d4640db257f8c7f5dd6ea1f76f.jpg[/img]
Next, we’ve completely overhauled the missile system. Due to the poor performance of missiles in the previous version, we’ve conducted a full reconstruction. Starting with shipboard missiles, we’ve introduced a concept similar to vertical launching, where launch positions are determined by the ship's hull and section configuration. Once a target is locked, the HUD will display the missile’s status. Hold the lock button (E) to begin targeting, and release it to fire the appropriate number of missiles. Warships can now carry multiple types of missiles and switch between them during combat to achieve different tactical objectives. However, shipboard missiles do have limited ammunition.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/2c8c424f48f41f9e875c87ad9279ab706e30ff39.jpg[/img]
Additionally, we’ve added sub turret missiles, which have some homing capabilities and are particularly effective against smaller units. Currently in testing, these sub turret missiles feature a trajectory similar to cold-launch systems. We’ve also restructured the missile trajectory logic, allowing missiles to create multi-stage, mixed-type trajectories, increasing tactical diversity.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/88bd274a78403d941f1449aa0c49a955fa7ae667.jpg[/img]
In terms of weapon systems, we experimented with configuring a test ship’s wing guns to all face forward, but the previous logic didn’t support this aiming style. We’ve now successfully implemented this feature, laying the groundwork for future "axial" superweapons.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/628775f0b21c080a7c07b12087d27ce7b45f8fe6.png[/img]
We hope you’ll enjoy these changes. If you have any feedback or suggestions, please share them in the comments. Thank you all for your support!

notes.title: TheFlagship Devlog#4
notes.notes:
Commanders, this update focuses primarily on interface optimization and combat experience improvements. Let me take you through the details.

First, we've improved target locking. The aircraft's target frame has been changed from above the aircraft to a dynamic circle around it, reducing HUD position interference during aiming. Additionally, distant aircraft will now be automatically filtered, minimizing distractions while targeting. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/b837ebe55654f5116bba1a657da12af11b72c231.png[/img]
On the warship side, the HUD in the previous version appeared somewhat bulky and obstructive. It has now been adjusted to a more streamlined circular outline, making the interface cleaner and less obstructive.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/82c02a5fe3013e463354f6f8010b7f19bf157809.png[/img]
Next, we've optimized shooting feedback. Both primary and secondary weapon hits will now have on-screen indicators, allowing you to clearly see which weapon successfully hit the target. The main cannon's reticle has undergone significant changes. It is now square-shaped, with the outer ring displaying the reload progress of the turret. The color will change based on aiming status, and firing will include dynamic effects, making the shooting process feel more precise. 

The direction indicator for the wing guns has been optimized to show module charging status. A yellow color indicates reloading, and a flash will occur once reloading is complete, helping you better determine the timing for your shots.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/223cb44ede47a26b9db0709c90e11f68ddea74ef.png[/img]
In terms of combat assistance, when using wing guns, if you continue to rotate while aiming with the right mouse button, the ship will automatically adjust its direction to help you maintain your target. When using the main cannon, once a target is locked, the main cannon reticle will activate dynamic tracking. While it won't fully lock onto the target's predicted position, it will reduce the pressure of aiming and increase your hit rate.

For the combat interface, we've added a centralized damage indicator that flashes red when you're hit, helping you quickly identify the source of the damage. The health bar has been changed to a top-down silhouette of the warship, with numerical health values now displayed. Additionally, when the number of available turrets for a specific weapon type reaches zero, the icon in the bottom right corner will automatically hide, keeping your view unobstructed. Lastly, we've introduced a new combat interface layout for A/B testing.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/6c1073b04958c13b4269247c15e23b512da5bab9.png[/img]
These changes should make combat smoother and operation feedback clearer. Future updates will continue to refine more details, so stay tuned to our patch notes to see what new features will be available next. We hope these improvements will make combat more intuitive for you.

 Don't forget to leave your thoughts and feedback in the comments. I'm NeveraiN, and we'll see you next time.

notes.title: TheFlagShip Devlog #1
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! Since I released my first game progress video, more and more people have started to notice my little project. I'm really happy about it~ In the past two weeks, the wish list has been growing slowly. I feel there are still many aspects of the store page that can be optimized, but that's something for later.
Let's get back to what I've done in these two weeks. First, I optimized the space jump effect within the syste. Now, the operation of heading to the next conflict point involves roughly aligning the ship's bow towards the conflict point and then initiating the jump.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/42b70a507cfd75a999768fcea7365336c00bf828.png[/img]
In some of the previous feedbacks, there was a desire for more in-depth ship customization. However, I've been struggling to find a suitable method until a friend suggested I take a look at the ship outfitting in "Stellaris." After researching it, I found it to be a perfect fit! So, I've implemented it!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/9ad05c63c03bc9830d16b3f8e224275ce6410512.png[/img]
Now, different class of warships will have varying numbers of sections. In addition to the equipment slots and gun positions on the hull itself, these sections will also provide equipment slots and gun positions. Players can switch sections to make the same warship has completely different combat styles!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/21e056d924badc4a21d4ab0ae1fbbda47bb4dd99.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45355348/eb8a08c33e1d27fcaa74450e3c4f50416497da27.png[/img]
